LESSON: SLAVERY AND SERVITUDE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: People and Relationships
Topic 2.3: Slavery and Servitude

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Slavery and Servitude. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why has slavery and servitude existed for thousands of years?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society
2. explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SLAVERY AND SERVITUDE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Slavery and Servitude helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SLAVERY AND SERVITUDE
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Slavery and Servitude” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade

What this means
In this part you learn to explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Slavery and Servitude.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Slavery and Servitude is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Slavery and Servitude” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Slavery and Servitude. (skill: explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Slavery and Servitude to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society.
3. Practise this skill: explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Slavery and Servitude from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Slavery and Servitude: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Slavery and Servitude?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why has slavery and servitude existed for thousands of years?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Slavery and Servitude means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the various forms of slavery and servitude in traditional African and contemporary society.
5. Be able to: explain factors that led to the development of the Indian Ocean slave trade.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
